## What you did
- Traced Orbitly's ~8% iOS funnel drop to the #240 dedupe. SDK kestrel-ios 3.2.0 sends a per-session `event_id`, so distinct events were dropped. About 1.18M legitimate Orbitly events were lost since 13/11 [1][2]. Zest's pilot lost 3,812 the same way [1].
- Wrote the fix: dedupe keyed on project, device and `event_id`, with replay tests kept. Opened PR #247 with Maya as reviewer [1][2].
- Drafted a note asking the iOS team to restore UUID `event_id`s in 3.2.1 [1].

## What changed
- Maya approved the logic on #247 once CI is green [2].
- Rachel confirmed Zest's dashboards are complete after the backfill and is closing their Zendesk ticket [6].
- The final 12/11 postmortem is up. Noa presents it at Friday's incident review (20/11) [3][7].

## What is still open
- Maya needs the Orbitly drop count for Thursday's call: about 1.18M real events, or ~8.1% of their iOS volume since 13/11 [1][2].
- Once #247 is merged and deployed, replay Orbitly from 13/11 (about 40 minutes), then Zest. Don't run it before the deploy, or the old key drops the events again [1].
- The iOS SDK note is still a draft. Nothing shows it was sent or that 3.2.1 is planned [1].
- Your Fathom action: add an alert when the ingest dead-letter queue exceeds 1,000 messages, before Friday's review [7].
